questions.q: When one light ray is reflected from a plane mirror with $30 °$ angle of reflection, the angle of deviation of the ray after reflection is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
& It is given that& $i = 30 °$.

The formula for angle of deviation is~
$\delta = 180 ° - 2i$

Substituting the values,
$\delta = 180 ° - 60 °$
$= 120 °$

questions.q: The difference of speed of light in the two media $A$ and $B \left({v}_{A} - {v}_{B}\right) is $2 . 6 $\times {10}^{7}$ms^{- 1}$. If the refractive index of medium $B$ is $1 . 47$, then the ratio of refractive index of medium $B$ to medium $A$ is: (Given : speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1})
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The speed of light in the medium& $B$~will be,~${v}_{B} = \dfrac{c}{\muB}$

The speed of light in the medium~$A$~will be,~${v}_{A} = \dfrac{c}{\muA}$.

Now,~

${v}_{A} - {v}_{B} = c\left(\dfrac{1}{\muA} - \dfrac{1}{\muB}\right) ⇒ 2 . 6 \times {10}^{7} = 3 \times {10}^{8} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{\muA} - \dfrac{1}{1 . 47}\right) ⇒ {μ}_{A} = 1 . 13$

questions.q: The graph shows how the magnification $m$ produced by a thin lens varies with image distance $v$. The focal length of the lens used is

For a thin lens,

From the above equation, slope of the line is~$\dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{c}{b} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

questions.q: For an object placed at a distance $2 . 4m$~from a lens, a sharp focused image is observed on a screen placed at a distance $12$ cm~from the lens. A glass plate of refractive index $1 . 5$~and thickness $1$ cm& is introduced between lens and screen such that the glass plate plane faces parallel to the screen. By what distance should the object be shifted so that a sharp focused image is observed again on the screen?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Given: object using the lens formula: \(\begin{aligned}& $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v \prime}-\frac{1}{w^{\prime}}$\\\Rightarrow & $\frac{21}{240} \mathrm{~cm}=\frac{3}{35} \mathrm{~cm}-\frac{1}{u^{\prime}}$\\\Rightarrow $\frac{1}{u^{\prime}}$& $=\frac{3}{35} \mathrm{~cm}-\frac{21}{240} \mathrm{~cm}$\\\Rightarrow & $\frac{1}{u^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{5}  \left[\frac{3}{7} \mathrm{~cm}-\frac{21}{48} \mathrm{~cm}\right]$\\\Rightarrow $\frac{1}{u^{\prime}}$ \text{ and } $=\frac{1}{5}  \left[\frac{144-147}{336}\right]$\\\Rightarrow u^{\prime} & =-560 $\mathrm{~cm}=-$5.6 $\mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$\) Hence, the object should be at \(5.6 $\mathrm{~m}$\) in front of the lens. Hence, the oblect should be moved by 5.6-24= \(3.2 $\mathrm{~cm}$\).

questions.q: A convex mirror of radius of curvature $30$ cm forms an image that is half the size of the object. The object distance is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given $R = 30cm$

So, $f = \dfrac{R}{2} = + 15cm$

For convex mirror, virtual image is formed for real object. Thus, magnification \left(m\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The magnification can be written as

$m = - \dfrac{v}{u} . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation (1) implies that

\dfrac{1}{2} = - \dfrac{v}{u}$⇒ v = - $\dfrac{u}{2}

The relation between the object distance, image distance and the focal length of the mirror is given by

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equation (2) implies that

\dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{- \dfrac{u}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{u} = - \dfrac{1}{u}$⇒ u = - 15cm$

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of $12$ cm in front of a plane mirror. The virtual and erect image is formed by the mirror. Now the mirror is moved by $4$ cm towards the stationary object. The distance by which the position of image would be shifted, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: When an object is placed in front of a plane mirror, object distance is equal to the image distance. In the first case, the image distance will be& $12$ cm~from the mirror. In the next case, as the mirror is moved towards the object, the object distance becomes~$8$ cm. Hence, image distance will also be~$8$ cm.

questions.q: What is the relative decrease in focal length of a lens for an increase in optical power by 0.1 D from 2.5D ? ['D' stands for dioptre]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P=\frac{1}{f} \\ & \text { So } P_1=\frac{1}{F_1} \Rightarrow F_1=\frac{1}{2.5} \\ & \text { Next } F_2=\frac{1}{2.6} \\ & \left|\frac{\Delta F}{F_1}\right|=\frac{\left|F_2-F_1\right|}{F_1}=\left|\frac{F_2}{F_1}-1\right| \\ & \Rightarrow\left|\frac{\Delta F}{F_1}\right|=\left|\frac{2.5}{2.6}-1\right|=\frac{0.1}{2.6} \approx 0.04\end{aligned}$

Now for~$TIR, $\theta$> {θ}_{C}$

questions.q: A concave mirror has radius of curvature of $40cm .$ It is at the bottom of a glass that has water filled up to $5$ cm (see figure). If a small particle is floating on the surface of water, its image as seen, from directly above the glass, is at a distance $d$ from the surface of water. The value of $d$ is close to: (Refractive index of water $= 1.33 )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given
$u = - 5cm$
$f = \dfrac{- R}{2} = - \dfrac{40}{2} = - 20cm$
Now
$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{- 20} = 1 \left(-5\right)$
$∴ \text{v} = + $\dfrac{20}{3}$cm$
Then
Object distance $d = 5 + $\dfrac{20}{3} = \dfrac{35}{3}$cm$ (below water surface)
The image after refraction
$d' = d \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{2}}{{\mu}_{1}}\right)$
$= \dfrac{35}{3} \left(\dfrac{1}{1.33}\right)
$= 8.77$
$d^{'} ≃ 8.8cm

questions.q:
In a medium the speed of light wave decreases to $0 . 2$~times to its speed in free space. The ratio of relative permittivity to the refractive index of the medium is $x: 1$. The value of $x$ is ______.

(Given speed of light in free space $= 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ and for the given medium ${μ}_{r} = 1$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Speed of light in medium is related to speed of light in vacuum \left(c\right)$~and refractive index~ \left(\mu\right)$~by~$v = \dfrac{c}{μ}$.

Then, we have~$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{c}{0 . 2c}$

$⇒ \mu = 5$

Refractive index in terms of~relative permeability \left({μ}_{r}\right)$and relative permittivity \left({ε}_{r}\right)$~ of the medium is stated as~$\mu = \sqrt{{ϵ}_{r}{μ}_{r}}$

$⇒ {ϵ}_{r} = \dfrac{\mu2}{\mur}$

$∴ \dfrac{ϵr}{μ} = \dfrac{μ}{\mur} = 5$

Hence, the value of~$x = 5$.

questions.q: The distance between object and its $3$ times magnified virtual image as produced by a convex lens is $20cm .$ The focal length of the lens used is ________ $cm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The image will be formed on the same side as the object. Therefore, $v = 3u$

Given: \left|v – u\right| = 20cm$

$⇒ \left|2u\right| = 20cm$

$⇒ u = - 10cm$ (-ve sign as the object is real)

From lens formula, we can write

$\dfrac{1}{( - 30 )} - \dfrac{1}{( - 10 )} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ f = 15cm$

$

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length $20$ cm is placed in front of convex mirror with principal axis coinciding each other. The distance between the lens and mirror is $10$ cm. A point object is placed on principal axis at a distance of $60$ cm from the convex lens. The image formed by combination coincides the object itself. The focal length of the convex mirror is _____~$cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For lens& $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} - 1\left(- 60\right) = \dfrac{1}{20} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$v = 30cm$

For the~final image to be formed on the object itself, after refraction from lens the ray should meet the mirror perpendicularly and the image by lens should be on the centre of curvature of mirror.

$R = 30 - 10 = 20cm$.

Now the focal length of mirror ${f}_{m} = \dfrac{R}{2} = 10cm$

questions.q: A ray of light passing through a prism& $( \mu = \sqrt{3} )$& suffers minimum deviation. It is found that the angle of incidence is double the angle of refraction within the prism. Then, the angle of prism is & (in degrees).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At minimum deviation,& ${r}_{1} = {r}_{2} = \dfrac{A}{2}$

Also given~$i = 2{r}_{1} = A$
Now~$1 \cdot sini = \sqrt{3}sin{r}_{1}$
$1sinA = \sqrt{3}sin\dfrac{A}{2}$

$⇒ 2sin\dfrac{A}{2}cos\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{3}sin\dfrac{A}{2}$
$⇒ cos\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{A}{2} = 30 °$
$⇒ A = 60 °$
